intervention: Idealized conveyor-like drive: prescribe only free-joint world-x velocity before each physics substep, smoothstep ramp 0.5 to 1.0s. No position writes, no return. Other five free-joint velocities and all contacts remain physical. Permanently release drive on simultaneous contact with both fingerpad groups; this proxy does not establish stable lifted grasp. Static control has no velocity or position writes.
primary: Task success versus execution interval K, five signed drive speeds, eight identical initial states per point.
secondary: Measured actual can velocity and distance; friction makes actual velocity lower than imposed pre-substep command
First unilateral finger contact vs bilateral grasp proxy; latched release
Paired success differences vs free static baseline
limits: One task, one policy seed and eight initial-state clusters; exploratory uncertainty is large
Idealized driven velocity disturbance, not a real conveyor or calibrated external force
The prescribed velocity is not the realized speed after friction and contact; report both
Drive release uses bilateral fingerpad contact as grasp proxy, not proof of secure grasp
Simulator pauses during inference; not real-time deployment
Policies can differ before motion onset; evaluates whole closed-loop execution schemes
